transport: M12 single-pole connector on the top panel · External Feedback Signal (EFS) · referenced to battery negative, output at battery-positive voltage, max 250 mA · Victron part number SPR00310 for the mating connector, included with the battery
blocks: One signal, two configurable functions. Default: External Feedback Signal — asserted on the battery's internal fault flags for redundant system protection. Alternative, enabled in VictronConnect: External Charging Signal (ECS) — the EFS output is held continuously high at battery-positive and drops on the low-SoC pre-alarm, giving a steady ON/OFF level that can drive a charger or contactor directly.

gotchas: This is a single wire, not a protocol. It is recorded because it is the only WIRED route into an NG SuperPack, and because in ECS mode it is genuinely useful: a level that says 'start charging' with no bus, no key and no pairing.
EFS sits at battery-positive when asserted — 12.8 V or 25.6 V. Same GPIO hazard as the BMS dry contacts: divide or opto-isolate, and size for the bank, not for 12 V.
250 mA is the ceiling. It drives a relay coil or a charger remote input, not a load.

EFS and ECS are alternative configurations of one output, selected in VictronConnect. A hub reading the wire cannot tell which mode the battery is in — that is a commissioning fact somebody has to write down.

These batteries also advertise Bluetooth Instant Readout with an unknown record type — see unknown-victron-ble-instant-readout. BLE would carry far more than this wire does, once somebody identifies the record.
unmappedReports: Low-SoC pre-alarm as a signal — no MetricKind. The ECS mode turns 'the bank is getting low' into a wire the hub can read, and there is no metric to receive it into., Internal fault flags (the EFS default trigger, described by the manual as covering rare fail-short scenarios of the internal switching devices) — no MetricKind for a battery fault code.
